Set defaults for apa7 package

Source: R/formatting.R
apa7_defaults.Rd

Sets options that apply to all apa7 tables. Settings that are not given are left as they are.

Usage

apa7_defaults(
  accuracy = NULL,
  font_family = NULL,
  font_size = NULL,
  line_spacing = NULL,
  intercept_text = NULL,
  column_formats = NULL,
  number_formatter = NULL,
  trim_leading_zero = NULL,
  width_aware_padding = NULL,
  page_width = NULL,
  landscape_width = NULL,
  column_width = NULL,
  table_width = NULL,
  print = NULL,
  citations = NULL,
  reset = FALSE
)

Arguments

accuracy

rounding accuracy of numbers in tables (default: .01, for two decimals). Model tables such as apa_parameters() and apa_anova() use it. Descriptive tables such as apa_descriptives(), apa_cor(), and apa_loadings() have their own digits argument instead (digits = 2 is the same as accuracy = .01).

font_family

font family

font_size

font size of tables and their notes, in points (default: 12)

line_spacing

spacing between the lines of tables' headers and bodies: 2 (default) for double spacing, 1.5, or 1 for single spacing. APA style allows any of these in tables. Table notes are always single-spaced.

intercept_text

label of the intercept row in regression tables (default: "Constant")

column_formats

a column_formats() object: the headers, formatters, and note definitions of table columns

number_formatter

function that formats numbers that can exceed 1 in absolute value (e.g., coefficients, standard errors, and test statistics). It takes a numeric vector and accuracy and returns a character vector. By default, align_chr() with the accuracy setting.

trim_leading_zero

function that formats numbers that cannot exceed 1 in absolute value (e.g., correlations, standardized coefficients, and R^2^), which APA style writes without a leading zero. By default, align_chr() with trim_leading_zeros = TRUE. Note that this is a function, unlike the TRUE/FALSE trim_leading_zeros argument of align_chr().

width_aware_padding

if TRUE (default), align_chr() pads text to equal rendered width in font_family (when the font is installed). If FALSE, text is padded with one figure space per missing character.

page_width

width of the text area of a portrait page, which tables fill with table_width = "page" (or 1, by default): a number (in inches) or the name of a paper size, whose width less APA's 1-inch margins on each side is used (e.g., "us-letter" gives 6.5 inches, the default, and "a4" gives 6.27 inches). If not set, the width comes from the paper and margins of the document being rendered, if any (see Details). Paper sizes are those of Typst's page function (e.g., "a4", "a5", "us-letter", "us-legal", "jis-b5"); see https://typst.app/docs/reference/layout/page/#parameters-paper.

landscape_width

width of the text area of a landscape page, in inches, which tables fill with table_width = "landscape". If NA (default), the height of the paper named by page_width less 1-inch margins (9 inches for "us-letter" and 9.69 inches for "a4"). When page_width is a number, the paper is taken to have the proportions of letter-size paper.

column_width

width of one column of a two-column page, in inches, which tables fill with table_width = "column". If NA (default), the width of a column in apaquarto's two-column journal mode (documentmode: jou): the paper width less 0.75-inch margins, less a gutter of 4% between the columns, divided by 2 (3.36 inches for "us-letter" and 3.25 inches for "a4"). When page_width is a number, the paper is taken to be that number plus 1-inch margins.

table_width

default width of tables, in any of the forms that the table_width argument of apa_flextable() takes: 1 (default) for the full width of a portrait page, a proportion of it (e.g., .8), "page", "landscape", "column", or a named number (e.g., c(column = 1)). In a two-column document, table_width = "column" makes tables as wide as a column, and a proportion given to a table function is then a proportion of the column. If not set, tables in a document in apaquarto's journal mode (documentmode: jou) are as wide as a column.

print

how tables made by apa7 functions (see apa7_tbl) are displayed: "auto" (default) as tables in Quarto and R Markdown documents and as tibbles in the console, "flextable" as tables everywhere, or "tibble" as tibbles everywhere

citations

how articles cited in table notes are written: "auto" (default), "keys", or "text". See apa7_write_bib().

reset

if TRUE, reset all defaults (except as specified)

Value

the previous values of the settings that were changed (all of them with reset = TRUE), invisibly, as a list that restores them when passed back to apa7_defaults() (e.g., with do.call())

Details

Each setting except column_formats, number_formatter, and trim_leading_zero is stored as an R option (e.g., apa7_defaults(page_width = "a4") sets options(apa7.page_width = "a4")), so it can also be set with options(), including in an .Rprofile file that runs at the start of every R session, before apa7 is loaded:

ArgumentOptionDefault
accuracyapa7.accuracy.01
font_familyapa7.font_family"Times New Roman"
font_sizeapa7.font_size12
line_spacingapa7.line_spacing2
intercept_textapa7.intercept_text"Constant"
width_aware_paddingapa7.width_aware_paddingTRUE
page_widthapa7.page_width6.5
landscape_widthapa7.landscape_widthNA (from page_width)
column_widthapa7.column_widthNA (from page_width)
table_widthapa7.table_width1
printapa7.print"auto"
citationsapa7.citations"auto"

column_formats, number_formatter, and trim_leading_zero are objects that need apa7 to be loaded, so they are set only with apa7_defaults() and last for the R session.

When page_width and table_width are not set, a Quarto or R Markdown document being rendered supplies them: its papersize sets the paper, and apaquarto's documentmode sets the margins (0.75 inches on each side in journal mode, jou, and 1.5 inches on the left in thesis mode). In journal mode, which sets the text in two columns, tables are as wide as a column by default. A setting made with apa7_defaults() or options() overrides the document.

The default column formats follow accuracy: changing it (with apa7_defaults() or the apa7.accuracy option) changes the number of decimals in tables. Setting column_formats without accuracy makes the formats' own accuracy the accuracy setting.

Examples

old <- apa7_defaults(accuracy = .001)

# Tables as wide as the text on A4 paper with 1-inch margins
apa7_defaults(page_width = "a4")

# A two-column document: tables are as wide as a column unless a table
# asks for another width (e.g., table_width = "page" in apa_flextable())
apa7_defaults(table_width = "column")

# Restore the earlier accuracy
do.call(apa7_defaults, old)

# Reset to package defaults
apa7_defaults(reset = TRUE)
